Pydantic Models

Smarter API MCPClient Manifest Constants.

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.const.DEFAULT_API_KEY_HEADER = 'X-API-Key'

Default HTTP header that carries the credential of an MCPClient whose authType is api_key.

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.const.DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL = 300

its tools, instructions and capabilities.

Type:

Default seconds to cache an MCP server’s catalog

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.const.DEFAULT_PRIORITY = 100

Default resolution order of an MCPClient.

Lower runs first.

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.const.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 30

Default seconds to wait for an MCP server to connect and respond.

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.const.MAX_CACHE_TTL = 86400

Maximum seconds to cache an MCP server’s catalog.

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.const.MAX_HEADERS = 20

Maximum number of custom HTTP headers.

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.const.MAX_HEADER_VALUE_LENGTH = 1024

Maximum length of a custom HTTP header value.

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.const.MAX_TIMEOUT = 120

Maximum seconds to wait for an MCP server to connect and respond.

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.const.RESERVED_HEADERS = frozenset({'authorization', 'connection', 'content-length', 'content-type', 'cookie', 'host', 'keep-alive', 'proxy-authorization', 'te', 'trailer', 'transfer-encoding', 'upgrade'})

Headers that a manifest may not set.

Credentials belong in a Smarter Secret, via credentials, and the rest are managed by the HTTP client and the MCP transport, as are all headers that begin with mcp-.

model_post_init(context, /)

This function is meant to behave like a BaseModel method to initialize private attributes.

It takes context as an argument since that’s what pydantic-core passes when calling it.

Return type:

None

Parameters:

  • self – The BaseModel instance.

  • context – The context.

Smarter API Manifest - MCPClient.spec.

An MCPClient connects Smarter to a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. When an LLMClient lists the MCPClient in its spec.mcpClients, the server’s tools are offered to the LLM on each prompt, alongside the LLMClient’s Plugins and Functions, and the server’s instructions are added to the system prompt.

spec:
  config:
    transport: http              # http (Streamable HTTP) or sse (legacy HTTP+SSE)
    endpointUrl: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
    headers: {}                  # optional, non-secret HTTP headers
    timeout: 30                  # seconds
    authType: bearer_token       # none, api_key, bearer_token or oauth2
    credentials: example_token   # the name of a Smarter Secret containing the credential
    apiKeyHeader: X-API-Key      # the header that carries an api_key credential
    allowedTools: []             # glob patterns. Empty means all of the server's tools
    allowedResources: []         # glob patterns of resource URIs the LLM may read
    includeInstructions: true    # add the server's instructions to the system prompt
    cacheTtl: 300                # seconds to cache the server's tools and instructions
    isActive: true
    priority: 100                # lower runs first

Note

Experimental. The MCPClient was designed and coded by Claude Code (Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5), with Lawrence McDaniel as co-author. It is experimental, and will be documented.

smarter.apps.mcpclient.manifest.models.mcpclient.spec.validate_endpoint_url(url)[source]

Validate an MCP server’s endpoint URL.

The URL must be https, on the standard port, without credentials or a fragment. Whether its host has a public address is verified each time Smarter connects.

Parameters:

url (str) – The URL.

Return type:

str

Returns:

The URL.

Raises:

SAMValidationError – If the URL is not permitted.
